propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired files, then commits non-atomically; if the worker is interrupted before commit, the working tree is left dirty with untracked regenerable artifacts.

The next reconverge union-merge runs 'git merge origin/tickets'; when origin has already pushed those *.retired/SNAPSHOT paths, the merge must create them but they exist untracked in the worktree, causing git to abort with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'.
Push-recovery cannot clear untracked files because 'git reset --hard' only affects tracked files and 'git stash create' is called without the -u flag.
Every merge retry aborts identically, wedging the store and stranding local commits off origin until manual intervention.

The fix detects the untracked-overwrite abort, parses the exact paths git names, relocates them to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, and retries the merge once; genuine content conflicts still abort as before.

Tracked .archived files deleted during compaction remain in 'git status' output as worktree deletions, causing plan-review and completion-verification gates to fail with store-read-failure even after writes are unwedged.
